references.text: In [ref:Luk 22:18|Luke 22:18], Jesus repeats a similar statement about the wine: he will not drink of the fruit of the vine until God's kingdom comes. Together with verse 16, this emphasizes that the Passover meal points forward to the fulfillment in God's kingdom.

In [ref:Luk 22:29-30|Luke 22:29-30], Jesus promises that his disciples will eat and drink at his table in his kingdom, which connects to the promise of the Passover meal being fulfilled in God's kingdom.

[ref:Matt 26:29|Matthew 26:29] is a parallel where Jesus says he will not drink of the fruit of the vine until he drinks it anew in his Father's kingdom. This is the same eschatological perspective as in Luke 22:16.

[ref:Mark 14:25|Mark 14:25] is Mark's parallel where Jesus says he will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until the day he drinks it anew in God's kingdom, with the same future-oriented promise as in Luke 22:16.

In [ref:Luk 13:29|Luke 13:29], Jesus speaks of people who will come from east and west to sit at the table in God's kingdom. This messianic feast vision is the background for the promise that the Passover meal will find its fulfillment in God's kingdom.

In [ref:Luk 14:15|Luke 14:15], one of the guests exclaims: "Blessed is the one who will eat at the table in God's kingdom!" This reflects the Jewish expectation of the eschatological meal that Jesus refers to in 22:16.

In [ref:Jes 25:6-9|Isaiah 25:6-9], the great feast the Lord will hold for all peoples on Mount Zion is described. This Old Testament promise of the eschatological banquet is the background for Jesus' words about the fulfillment of the Passover meal in God's kingdom.

[ref:Åp 19:9|Revelation 19:9] speaks of the marriage supper of the Lamb and declares blessed those who are invited. This is the final fulfillment that Jesus points to when he says the Passover meal will be completed in God's kingdom.

In [ref:1 Kor 11:26|1 Corinthians 11:26], Paul writes that the Lord's Supper proclaims the Lord's death "until he comes". This underscores the same eschatological tension between the present meal and the future fulfillment that Jesus speaks of in Luke 22:16.

In [ref:2 Mos 12:14|Exodus 12:14], the Passover celebration is instituted as a permanent ordinance. Jesus connects to this tradition, but points out that the Passover will now find its final fulfillment (πληρωθῇ) in God's kingdom.
